title: The Verbena tale of creation
summary: How the Old Faith tells the birth of the Tellurian.

claims.text: In Verbena lore the One became Two, Goddess and God, and from their union came the Tellurian and the turning of the Great Wheel.
Through humanity the Tellurian came to see and know itself, and because it cherished humankind, fragments of the One called the Pure Ones came down to dwell in people.

title: The Burning Times
summary: The witch hunts as the Verbena remember them.

claims.text: Secret Inquisitors, at times backed by Christian mages, were the worst danger to the Verbena.
Most people killed as witches knew little real magic beyond charms, herb-lore and midwifery.
Only a handful of true Verbena died, but they were few to begin with, and each loss was felt as a wound to the Tree of Life.

title: Verbena sacred places in the Americas
summary: Nodes and holy sites the Verbena prize.

claims.text: Gallows Hill in Salem, where accused witches were hanged, is a place of power, and public rituals there hide the odd real working.
Nodes lie in the Berkshires and Ozarks, and the Pacific Northwest keeps several, including sacred springs such as Breitenbush and Cougar.
Verbena see the Amazon as a cradle of life and fight its destruction by the Syndicate, with help from Dreamspeakers and sorcerers.

title: Gardeners of the Tree
summary: Verbena traditionalists who keep the Old Ways.

claims.text: Gardeners claim a line back to the Aeduna and the Wyck, and their account is the accepted history of the Tradition.
Early Gardeners feared their family secrets would be diluted and wanted the Tradition kept to those with the gift in their blood.
They still admit chosen outsiders to renew the old families.

title: Twisters of Fate
summary: Spinners who claim the oldest power of the Wyck.

claims.text: Verbena scholars think Wyck meant both wise and to twist or shape, fitting folk who bent reality to their will.
Twisters say the first of their kind were early shamans, wise women and healers who held shards of the Pure Ones.
Those shamans merged with the Aeduna and were long indistinguishable from other mages of the Old Faith.

title: Moon-Seekers
summary: The eclectic seekers of the Verbena.

claims.text: If Gardeners are the trunk and Twisters the roots, the Moon-Seekers are the leaves of the Tree, some say its fruits and nuts.
Pagan visionaries who saw the Order of Reason as an enemy of all of them united the Old Faiths and may have saved them from the Burning Times.
Wandering Moon-Seekers gather wisdom from peoples across the world to enrich the Tradition.

title: Lifeweavers
summary: Wild Verbena who side with the predator.

claims.text: Lifeweavers see nature as beyond good and evil, simply what it is, and they identify most with nature's predators.
Other factions, chiefly the Gardeners, coined the name for Verbena who fit nowhere else; it remains a scatter of loners more than a group.
In the Mythic Ages they were hermits of the wilds who warned off even fellow pagans, joining the Verbena only as the Order of Reason closed in.

title: Elements and blood in Verbena magic

claims.text: Cords and threads stand for strands of fate, serve in fate spells and bind a spell's subject.
Earth, air, fire and water are used as symbols and as sympathetic links, usually tied to north, east, south and west, though some swap air and fire.
Blood, the mage's own or a sacrifice's, is a strong focus because it carries life and links to its source.
